chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl al-Basri, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I wrote to him: 'Does the executor purify [pay zakat] on behalf of the orphans with the Zakat of al-Fitra if they have wealth?' So he wrote: 'There is no zakat upon an orphan.'

And [he asked] about a slave whose master dies while he is absent from him in another city, and in his hand is wealth belonging to his master, and the time for Fitra arrives: 'Can he purify [pay zakat] on behalf of himself from the wealth of his master, and it has already gone to the orphans?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat of al-Fitra (obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat al-Fitra obligatory on orphans and slaves?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of Zakat al-Fitra by establishing that orphans are exempt from this obligation, reflecting the principle that Zakat is a purification of surplus wealth rather than a burden on dependents. It further details the specific scenario where a slave, possessing personal wealth while his master is absent, is permitted to pay Zakat on his own behalf using his master's funds, highlighting the flexibility in managing household assets during the festive period.
